header.status_line: Paradigm is coded on Mark 16: 17 named cultural templates (text-level) + 60/60 moves carry a per-move template-note. The dominant is 'vindication of the righteous sufferer' (salience 0.95). The paradigm NAME is emergent (named in the tradition's own terms, not from a fixed list, s2.1); the posture toward it (stance) and its relation to the dominant are closed enums.

what_it_is: Paradigm names the cultural SCRIPTS a text runs on -- the templates that pre-exist the text and give its content shape: a role-set, a set of relations between the roles, and an end the script is oriented toward. Mark 16 runs 'vindication-of-the-righteous-sufferer', 'empty-tomb / translation-of-the-hero', 'burial-anointing / mourning-rite' and more; it does not merely cite them, it ENDORSES some, INVOKES others, and SUBVERTS others (the women's mourning-rite is set up in full, then broken open by the absent body).
why_it_matters: A move can look unique until you see the template it is running. Paradigm is what lets two texts that share NO wording still share a script -- and it is where an absence speaks: a template a text could have invoked and did NOT (a paradigm it declines) is a coded silence. The stance + relation fields keep 'invokes' distinct from 'endorses' from 'subverts', so a text using a script AGAINST itself is not misread as affirming it.

how_it_works.you_give_it: a coded text (its moves, from Decompose).
how_it_works.the_method_does: names each cultural template the text runs on (emergent, in the tradition's own terms), marks the dominant one, scores each template's salience, and codes the text's stance toward it + its relation to the dominant paradigm.
how_it_works.you_get_back: a ranked set of named paradigms with stance + relation + salience, at text and move grain.

pipeline_context.note: sibling terms glossed so the card stands alone.
pipeline_context.move: one small action a text makes (agent does an operation to something, with a result) -- the unit Decompose produces.
pipeline_context.Decompose: the node that breaks a passage into moves; Paradigm (in Situate) runs alongside it.
pipeline_context.Situate: the parent node: attaches context to each move; Paradigm is its 'templates' aspect.
pipeline_context.the dominant paradigm: the highest-salience template the text runs on; the others are coded by how they RELATE to it.
pipeline_context.emergent (fit-or-extend): the paradigm NAME is not picked from a fixed list -- it is named in the tradition's own terms (s2.1 = do not pre-anchor), then reused if it recurs.
pipeline_context.salience: how strongly the template is in play in this text (0-1); not a confidence, a weight.
pipeline_context.PI: the principal investigator (the researcher) -- who locks methodology calls.

how_we_grade_it.Fidelity: mechanical: does every label map to a real source_paradigm column with in-vocab enum values?
how_we_grade_it.Cold Read: self-sufficiency: a blind reader judges whether the card explains itself.
how_we_grade_it.vs-Wild: does the coded paradigm-set beat a naive reader given the passage + 'what cultural scripts is this running?' (validated 2026-08-08, PASS — see the vs-Wild pill).

the_method_clean.note: Paradigm's fields: the NAME is open/emergent (s2.1); stance + relation_to_dominant are closed enums; salience + is_dominant are numeric/bool. Values render from the coded data (the enums are controlled-by-convention -- a formal vocab table is owed).

fields.note: OPEN / emergent -- the paradigm named in the tradition's own terms (115 distinct across the corpus)
the text's posture: endorsed (affirms it) / invoked (uses it) / subverted (sets it up then breaks it) / denied (rejects it)
vs the dominant template: reinforces / self (it IS the dominant) / competes / subverts / incompatible / ironizes
NUMERIC 0-1 -- how strongly the template is in play
OPEN -- the warrant for the reading

the_method_clean.controlled_by_convention: stance + relation_to_dominant are small fixed sets enforced by convention (no vocab table yet); OWED a live vocab source so they render live like Frame's.

the_method_applied.note: Mark 16's cultural templates (render-from-data): the TOP 5 of 17 by salience shown, each with its stance + relation-to-dominant + the evidence snippet. Distributions above cover all 17.

where_saved.plain: Text-level paradigms save to source_paradigm (@ the base key MARK-16); per-move templates to source_move.paradigm (@ the live moveset). Read the family via text_checkout, never a bare key.

honest_limits: The paradigm NAME is emergent (s2.1) -- a strength (it is the tradition's own script, not an imposed label) but it means names are not a closed set; cross-text paradigm-matching is a separate, later step.
stance + relation_to_dominant are controlled-by-convention (no formal vocab table + definitions the drawer reads live); OWED, like the other non-Frame closed enums.
One coder, one pass, engine-proposed; not reliability-tested. salience is a single-coder judgment.
Cold Read run 2026-08-11 (opus, cold) — PARTIAL; vs-Wild validated 2026-08-08 — PASS. Both render from card_check.
SCALE: coded on the worked text (Mark 16); 17 paradigms here. The corpus holds 115 distinct paradigm names, but this card is the Mark-16 worked example, not corpus coverage.
made_by: source_paradigm (the text-level paradigm store) + source_move.paradigm (the per-move template)
whats_next: Checks on the record: Cold Read PARTIAL (2026-08-15); vs-Wild PASS (2026-08-08, predates the current engine, so it is owed a re-run). Give stance + relation_to_dominant a live vocab source (the last owed vocab item). The vs-Wild PASS predates the S170 living-vocab engine and was WEB-only, so it is owed a rerun on an UNDERSTUDIED text (§2.14: Mark 16 compresses millennia of commentary, so naive parity there measures the model's memory, not the instrument). Cross-text paradigm-matching (which texts share a script) is a later comparative step, not this aspect.

leans_on: frame semantics (Fillmore) + cultural-script theory (a template of roles -> relations -> telos)
form criticism's Gattung / genre-script sense generalised cross-tradition
fit-or-extend emergent naming (s2.1) -- the paradigm is named in the tradition's own terms, not imposed
the stance/relation distinction leans on reception theory (a text can run a script to affirm OR to break it)

run_and_record._this_is_the_agent_spec: everything needed to RUN this engine and record a result, in one block. The rest of the card is written for a human reader; nothing there is required to act.

black_box_contract.reads: see the engine script's header contract.
black_box_contract.writes: see the engine script's header contract.
black_box_contract.upstream: Decompose (source_move) must already have run for this key; Situate refines an existing moveset.
black_box_contract.gates: the run tag names one run, never a text; CHECK-constrained values are coerced against the vocab SSOT before write; an empty model response fails loud rather than writing a partial batch.

run_and_record.how_to_read_the_pills: a pill is the verdict of one DATED run, not a live status; where it and the card body disagree, the body is current. whats_next is generated fresh on every build.

before_you_run.decompose_first: Situate codes a text Decompose has already broken into moves, and the move-grain aspects read that moveset directly. Against an empty moveset a run does not error, it silently produces nothing. Check: SELECT COUNT(*), MAX(run_tag) FROM source_move WHERE source_key='<key>';
before_you_run.the_text_file: --text-file takes plain UTF-8. The reproducible way to make one is the LIBRARY checkout (shared_terms.text_checkout); a hand-pasted file works once but flag it in evidence_basis.
before_you_run.the_card_builder_is_mark_16_only: the CODERS run on any text; the drawer BUILDERS have the Mark 16 keys hardcoded and take no arguments. A new text can be coded and queried today, but its card cannot be generated, so its Cold Read cannot run. The parameterised builder is owed.

naming_conventions.run_tag: <textslug>_s<session>_<YYYYMMDD>, e.g. mark16_s170_20260813. One tag per RUN, not per text, so a re-code never overwrites an older run. Lands in: source_paradigm has NO run_tag column: the tag is written into extraction_provenance as `tag=<run_tag>`. Filter with: WHERE extraction_provenance LIKE '%tag=<run_tag>%'. Older rows carry pre-convention tags (form_v1_s168, witness_s161, ood_s168) — historical, do not copy, and the reason a query must name its run.
naming_conventions.deployed_drawer_file: ../grammarofmeaning-site/engine/data/goldenpath/<text_slug>/paradigm_node_drawer.json — the SIBLING deploy repo (what other cards call DEPLOY_REPO), not this one. text_slug is the source_key lowercased without punctuation: MARK-16-WEB -> mark16, MARK-16-GRC -> mark16_grc, TTC-CH1-EN -> ttc_ch1. A new text needs its directory made first (mkdir -p).
naming_conventions.cold_read_run_doc: pm/30_methodology/engine/COLDREAD_situate_paradigm_run_<YYYY-MM-DD>.md — run_cold_read.py writes it and prints the path. Pass --date or the filename carries the wrong day.
naming_conventions.vs_wild_run_doc: pm/30_methodology/engine/VALIDATION_situate_paradigm_vs_wild_run_<YYYY-MM-DD>.md — YOU write this one. The runner only drops the wild arm in field_ed/_persona_engine/out/situate_vs_wild/; the comparison against the instrument arm is yours to write, and seed_card_check.py fails loud if the cited file is absent.
naming_conventions.the_account_flag: --account hds picks which Claude Max plan the SDK call uses (Tier 1, $0). Check it is live first: ./scripts/_run_python.sh scripts/lib/sdk_account_refresh.py hds --check

how_to_record_a_verdict.step_1: run the Cold Read: ./scripts/_run_python.sh scripts/analysis/run_cold_read.py --node situate.paradigm --drawer-file <the deployed drawer json for this text> --date <YYYY-MM-DD> --account hds  (it prints the COLDREAD run-doc path it wrote; see naming_conventions).
how_to_record_a_verdict.step_2: add ONE ROWS entry to scripts/analysis/seed_card_check.py of exactly this shape:

rows_entry_shape.run_doc: <the COLDREAD run-doc path run_cold_read.py just printed>

how_to_record_a_verdict.step_3: run ./scripts/_run_python.sh scripts/analysis/seed_card_check.py  (it FAILS LOUD unless the cited run_doc exists on disk); the verdict lands in card_check and renders as the pill. Seeding just means adding that ROWS entry and running the script: there is no other step.
how_to_record_a_verdict.the_bar: PASS = a fresh reader can RUN the engine from this card (Cold Read) and FIND where the prior work lives (Cold Start), with no broken gaps, honest limits flagged, and the card TIGHT — a reader should not be able to cut a third of it without loss. Not zero-clarifications: close the broken gaps, flag the limits, cut the padding, stop.

how_to_run_vs_wild.what_it_asks: does our scaffolding beat the same text read by an unscaffolded LLM given none of the instrument's fields. Primary metric is RELIABILITY (do repeated runs agree), not eloquence. Scope the wild arm to ONLY this aspect's job: an unscoped wild reader borrows the other layers' work and appears to win.
how_to_run_vs_wild.step_2_instrument_arm: this aspect's coded rows, already in its store. Comparison protocol: pm/30_methodology/engine/VALIDATION_situate_vs_wild_RUNSHEET_s170_2026-08-11.md.
how_to_run_vs_wild.step_3_record: record it like a Cold Read, with check_name 'vs_wild'.
how_to_run_vs_wild.for_a_new_text: PROMPTS in the runner is {aspect: prompt}; copy an entry and swap the text's name. It currently holds sitz / transmission / lineage, all written for Mark 16.
how_to_run_vs_wild.honest_limit: per §2.14 the DECISIVE run is on an UNDERSTUDIED text. On Mark 16 a naive model scores well from memory of the commentary, so parity there measures recall, not the instrument.

foundation_codes._what: the honesty tags on EVERY Situate coding, whatever wrote it. C4/R7 = evidence_basis + certainty (on what basis, how sure). C8/R3 = scope_level (at what grain). Grammar situate_foundation_v1, rendered from scripts/lib/situate_foundation_vocab.py.

evidence_basis (C4/R7).external-material: archaeology / epigraphy / material culture attests it.
evidence_basis (C4/R7).scholarly-consensus-with-citation: the field agrees AND a real citation is attached (corpus/DR only, never LLM memory).
evidence_basis (C4/R7).strongly-inferred: the coder reasoned it from strong, multi-source warrant (not from the coded text alone).
evidence_basis (C4/R7).internally-inferred: inferred FROM the text being coded — the context-laundering flag; downstream may EXCLUDE.
evidence_basis (C4/R7).LLM-proposed: a model proposed it with no external warrant (make the LLM-ness visible, §2.8).
evidence_basis (C4/R7).contested: the field actively disagrees; there is no settled basis.

certainty (C4/R7).low: the coder would not defend this value against a competing reading; treat as provisional.
certainty (C4/R7).med: the coder's best reading, but a competing reading is live (record it in alternative_hypothesis).
certainty (C4/R7).high: the coder would defend this value; no live competing reading at this grain.

scope_level (C8/R3).text: the whole source — the coding is a property of the work, not of any one part of it.
scope_level (C8/R3).pericope: the source's NATIVE sub-division (Mark 16:1-8 vs 16:9-20). Where no native division is marked, fall back to the Connect bundle / spine-segment — do NOT invent a new pericope primitive (R3).
scope_level (C8/R3).move: a single move (one operation plus its arguments), as produced by Decompose.

foundation_codes.alternative_hypothesis (C4/R7): OPEN free text: the competing reading the coder rejected. Expected whenever certainty is low or med.

codes_glossary.stance: invoked | endorsed | subverted (how the text uses the paradigm)

shared_terms.text_checkout: the LIBRARY's package of a text, and the mandated read path: verbatim (byte-identical to the stored passage text, hashed), anchored (carries {source_id, passage_id, verse_markers}), and versioned (a pinned snapshot). Engines code the checkout OFFLINE rather than reading the live DB, and results ingest back joined on the anchor. Build one with: ./scripts/_run_python.sh scripts/analysis/build_checkout_package_s162.py --source-id <id> --ref "Mark 16" --out <path>  (optional: --verse-prefix / --section-prefix to pick the in-text markers, --edition WEB, --version v1). It resolves a source already in-corpus and chunked.
shared_terms.move: one operation plus its arguments: the derived sense-unit Decompose produces. Distinct from a passage, which is the source's own container (verse, pericope, paragraph).
shared_terms.wild: an unscaffolded LLM read of the same text, given none of the instrument's fields. The control arm.

methodology_tags.§2.1: code from the text's own terms; do not force a pre-set label (anti-pre-anchoring).
methodology_tags.§2.8: bias-visibility: name the conditions so corpus skew stays auditable, not hidden.
methodology_tags.§2.14: test the method out-of-domain (an understudied text), not only the one it was tuned on.
methodology_tags.§2.16: render from data: the card is generated from the coding, so it cannot silently drift.
methodology_tags.§2.13: single store of record: canonical data lives in a DB table (mirrored to Neon), not a loose file.
